title: Fire & Rescue Service
summary: Capabilities of a UK fire and rescue service: prevention, fire safety regulation, emergency response, operational readiness and multi-agency resilience.
sourceDescription: Starter capability map for a UK fire and rescue service, kept neutral between the nations of the UK. Vocabulary drawn from public National Fire Chiefs Council, Fire Standards Board and HMICFRS materials (consulted for scope, not copied). Draft only: written by Claude and not yet reviewed by a named person with fire service experience.

sources.citation: National Fire Chiefs Council and Fire Standards Board public materials (consulted for vocabulary and scope; nothing copied)
HMICFRS fire and rescue service inspection framework (consulted for scope coverage; nothing copied)
UK Government Functional Standards GovS 001-016 (consulted for the shared corporate capabilities)

items.name: Spend Control & Compliance

items.name: Information Management

items.name: Records Management

items.name: Data Governance & Quality

items.name: Information Rights & Access

items.name: Data Protection & Privacy

items.name: Analytics & Business Intelligence

items.name: Customer Contact

items.name: Identity & Account Verification

items.name: Complaints & Feedback
items.description: Receiving, investigating and learning from complaints and compliments.

items.name: Accessibility & Inclusion

items.name: Estates

items.name: Property Portfolio & Strategy
items.description: Deciding which properties to hold, acquire, adapt or release.

items.name: Facilities & Building Operations
items.description: Running buildings day to day: cleaning, security, utilities and reception.

items.name: Maintenance & Compliance
items.description: Keeping buildings safe, compliant and in good repair over their life.

items.name: Space & Workplace
items.description: Allocating and configuring space to how people actually work.

items.name: Energy & Sustainability
items.description: Reducing the energy, carbon and environmental impact of the estate.

items.name: Digital & Technology
items.description: Delivering and running the technology and digital services the organisation depends on.

items.name: Enterprise Architecture & Standards
items.description: Setting the target technology landscape and the standards it follows.

items.name: Application Delivery & Support
items.description: Building, buying, integrating and supporting the applications the business runs on.

items.name: Infrastructure, Cloud & Networks
items.description: Providing the compute, storage, hosting and connectivity services rely on.

items.name: Cyber Security & Resilience
items.description: Protecting systems and data from threats and recovering from disruption.

items.name: Digital Service Design
items.description: Designing user-centred digital services around real user needs.

items.name: Technology Service Management

items.name: Governance & Assurance
items.description: Directing the organisation and assuring that it is well run, lawful and accountable.

items.name: Risk Management

items.name: Internal Audit & Assurance
items.description: Independently checking that controls work and reporting on them.

items.name: Legal & Regulatory Compliance
items.description: Meeting the laws, regulations and statutory duties that apply.

items.description: Operating the board, committees and scheme of delegation transparently.

items.name: Business Continuity & Emergency Planning

items.name: Prevention & Community Safety
items.description: Reducing the number and harm of fires and other emergencies by helping people stay safe.

items.name: Community Risk Profiling
items.description: Using local data to find the people and places most at risk of fire.

items.name: Home Fire Safety Visits
items.description: Visiting households to give advice, fit alarms and reduce fire risk.

items.name: Safety Education & Youth Engagement
items.description: Teaching children, young people and groups how to prevent and survive fires.

items.name: Road & Water Safety
items.description: Working with partners to reduce deaths and injuries on roads and near water.

items.name: Arson Reduction
items.description: Working with partners to reduce deliberate fires and their causes.

items.name: Protection & Fire Safety Regulation
items.description: Making sure buildings and events are safe and that responsible people meet their legal duties.

items.name: Premises Risk Inspection
items.description: Auditing buildings against fire safety law, focused on those at highest risk.

items.name: Building Regulations Consultation
items.description: Advising on the fire safety of new building and alteration plans.

items.name: Licensing & Events Advice
items.description: Advising on fire safety for licensed premises and public events.

items.name: Enforcement & Prosecution
items.description: Issuing notices and bringing prosecutions where fire safety duties are not met.

items.name: Fire Investigation
items.description: Establishing the cause and spread of fires and sharing what is learned.

items.name: Emergency Response & Mobilisation
items.description: Receiving emergency calls and sending the right crews and kit to protect life and property.

items.name: Emergency Call Handling & Mobilisation
items.description: Answering emergency calls and sending the nearest suitable resources.

items.name: Incident Command
items.description: Directing crews and partners safely at incidents of every size.

items.name: Firefighting & Rescue Operations
items.description: Fighting fires and rescuing people from fires, collisions and other danger.

items.name: Specialist Rescue & Hazardous Materials
items.description: Responding to water, height, collapse and chemical incidents with specialist crews and kit.

items.name: Response Standards & Station Cover
items.description: Setting how fast crews should arrive and keeping enough cover to meet it.

items.name: Operational Debrief & Learning
items.description: Reviewing incidents to capture lessons and update procedures.

items.name: Operational Readiness & Training
items.description: Making sure crews, vehicles and equipment are ready, safe and available when called.

items.name: Operational Training & Competence
items.description: Training firefighters and officers and keeping their skills assessed and current.

items.name: Firefighter Fitness & Wellbeing
items.description: Keeping operational staff medically and physically fit and supporting their wellbeing.

items.name: Fleet & Appliance Management
items.description: Buying, maintaining and replacing fire engines and other vehicles.

items.name: Equipment & PPE Management
items.description: Issuing, testing and maintaining operational equipment and protective clothing.

items.name: Water Supplies & Hydrants
items.description: Making sure hydrants and other water supplies are mapped, tested and usable.

items.name: On-Call Availability
items.description: Recruiting on-call firefighters and keeping their crewing levels reliable.

items.name: Resilience & Multi-Agency Planning
items.description: Preparing with other agencies for major incidents and keeping plans tied to local risk.

items.name: Community Risk Management Planning
items.description: Setting out the local risks and how the service will address them.

items.name: Multi-Agency Planning & Exercising
items.description: Planning and rehearsing joint responses with police, health, councils and others.

items.name: Major Incident Preparedness
items.description: Keeping the service ready for large, long-running or national-scale emergencies.

items.name: Operational Risk Information
items.description: Gathering and sharing site-specific hazard information for crews on the way to incidents.

valueStreams.name: Keep People Safe at Home
valueStreams.description: Starts when a household or community is identified as at risk. Ends when safety advice and equipment have been given and followed up.

valueStreams.name: Make Buildings Safe
valueStreams.description: Starts when a building or event needs a fire safety check. Ends when risks are fixed or enforced and the outcome is recorded.

valueStreams.name: Respond to an Emergency
valueStreams.description: Starts when an emergency call is received. Ends when the incident is closed and lessons are recorded.

valueStreams.name: Be Ready to Respond
valueStreams.description: Starts when crews, vehicles or equipment need to be ready for service. Ends when they are competent, available and fit for use.

valueStreams.name: Prepare with Partners
valueStreams.description: Starts when a local risk needs a joint plan. Ends when the plan has been exercised and improved.
